title: PZ Agent TeamON Bridge Message
description: One line of the voice bridge protocol, either direction. The transport is the child's stdin/stdout: one JSON object per line, UTF-8, at most 16384 bytes encoded. Four types travel to the bridge (hello, speak, interrupt, goal) and four travel from it (ready, transcript, outcome, error); a type on the wrong side is refused as firmly as an unknown one. The 'goal' message carries a token from a closed enum, never transcript text: the channel from a microphone to anything else is exactly that enum. The 'error' message's 'detail' is free text from the far end; a reader classifies 'code' and drops 'detail' unread, because every consumer of a fault eventually reaches a speech synthesiser.

v.description: The sender's protocol version, MAJOR.MINOR. A reader accepts any peer whose MAJOR matches its own; a MINOR difference is compatible.

oneOf.description: To the bridge: opens the session and declares this build's protocol version. No other fields.
To the bridge: one utterance to synthesise.

text.description: What to say. Refused empty and refused past the cap rather than truncated: an overlong utterance here is a bug on the sending side, and truncating would hide it mid-sentence.

oneOf.description: To the bridge: abandon one utterance now.
To the bridge: dispatch one goal token under a request id. The token set is closed on purpose — there is no field wide enough to carry a transcript.
From the bridge: answers hello with the bridge's own protocol version (the 'v' field). No other fields.

From the bridge: one recognition result, interim hypotheses included. A reader clamps rather than refuses: text is cut to 400 characters, at_ms floored at 0, confidence clamped to [0, 1] — a recogniser emitting accumulated context is doing something normal.

From the bridge: how one speak or one goal ended. 'ended' is the only status that claims the thing was carried out; failed, refused and cancelled are all 'it stopped', distinguished because the companion says something different about each.

From the bridge: a bridge-side failure. A reader turns 'code' into a fixed phrase and reads nothing else; 'detail' is where the far end's free text lives and it is dropped on the floor. A code a reader does not know is reported as an unknown failure rather than refused, because refusing the report of a failure loses the failure.

code.description: The closed set a current bridge emits. A reader must also survive a code outside this list (a newer bridge), which is why the schema documents the set without the reader enforcing it.

handle.description: An id minted by the companion: lowercase, 1 to 64 characters from letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore.
